pre_introduction_meta.title: 40k Reforged Listbuilder Project - Pre-Introduction for the Next AI
pre_introduction_meta.purpose: This document is the orientation layer for a new AI entering the 40k Reforged Listbuilder project. It should be read before the current handoff and before editing project files.
pre_introduction_meta.critical_length_instruction: THERE IS NO MAXIMUM LENGTH OR SIZE FOR THIS PRE-INTRODUCTION OR FOR PROJECT HAND-OFF MATERIALS.
pre_introduction_meta.why_completeness_matters: An omitted architectural assumption, proven New Recruit behavior, naming convention, or design principle can cause subtle regressions across many faction catalogues. A few extra kilobytes are cheaper than rediscovering or corrupting project knowledge.
pre_introduction_meta.instruction_to_next_ai: Do not compress this project into a generic BattleScribe/New Recruit task. Treat the supplied files and conventions as a mature, evolving system with deliberately tested UX, semantics, and maintenance architecture.
pre_introduction_meta.timelessness_rule: This document deliberately avoids live revision numbers, current faction status, immediate next tasks, and temporary reference implementations. Those belong in the current handoff and current project files.

project_at_a_glance.domain: New Recruit / BattleScribe-style JSON catalogues for the homebrew Warhammer 40k ruleset called 40k Reforged
project_at_a_glance.primary_goal: Build a clean, reliable, low-friction army listbuilder that acts as a companion to the authoritative army rules rather than attempting to reproduce the entire ruleset.
project_at_a_glance.secondary_goal: Maintain a reusable catalogue architecture and authoring grammar that can be applied consistently across factions without erasing meaningful faction-specific differences.
project_at_a_glance.maturity: This is a mature multi-faction system with shared infrastructure, reusable libraries, established New Recruit runtime knowledge, and a growing body of maintenance doctrine.
what_success_looks_like: A player can build an army quickly without wrestling with New Recruit implementation details.
The builder records meaningful final choices rather than mirroring every procedural replacement sentence from the PDF.
Illegal list states are either prevented cleanly or explained constructively.
The UI remains visually simple and readable.
The same class of mechanic is represented consistently across factions unless the game rules genuinely differ.
The project can be maintained without repeatedly rediscovering old decisions.

why_this_project_needs_orientation.starting_point: The project began as a relatively direct catalogue transcription exercise: units, categories, points, legal selections, and stock validation.
what_was_learned: Literal PDF transcription often produces poor listbuilding UX.
New Recruit data structures frequently expose implementation details rather than player decisions.
Apparently reasonable BattleScribe JSON can render as awkward spinners, redundant rows, blank wrappers, confusing nested menus, or implementation-language errors.
Clean UI and semantic legality do not always need to be enforced by the same object.
Some unusual structures exist because they were tested against actual New Recruit behavior and solved a real runtime problem.
why_this_project_needs_orientation.resulting_shift: The project evolved from 'encode the army rules into New Recruit' into 'design a disciplined translation layer between source semantics and the player's listbuilding experience.'
why_this_project_needs_orientation.important_warning: Do not normalize, flatten, simplify, or rewrite an unfamiliar structure merely because it looks odd in JSON. First determine what behavior it owns and whether the shape is intentional.

core_design_philosophy.fancy_notepad_not_rules_engine: The listbuilder is intended to replace a notepad, not the army rules PDF. It quickly records the choices that make up an army and catches illegal list construction without reproducing every battlefield rule, weapon profile, or procedural clause.
core_design_philosophy.meaningful_choices: Represent the decisions players actually make. Prefer clean final-state choices over procedural replacement chains when the resulting game meaning is exact.
core_design_philosophy.not_every_legal_option_needs_a_button: The builder should make common choices quick rather than give every technically legal option equal prominence. The army rules remain authoritative when an uncommon or default option is not represented.
core_design_philosophy.constructive_validation: When permissive-corrective validation is appropriate, prefer the three-part pattern: state the invalid condition, state the allowed condition, then state the repair.
core_design_philosophy.individual_consideration: Standardize the visual grammar and authoring conventions, but do not force unlike rules into identical shapes. Individual consideration beats blind homogenisation.

authority_hierarchy.principle: Different project sources own different kinds of truth. Do not let convenience or stale documentation silently override the correct authority.

order.source: Authoritative army rules PDF / Universal Unit Skeleton
order.owns: Game meaning, legal choices, points, unit identity, faction semantics, and player-facing source rules.
Reusable listbuilder doctrine, canonical shared infrastructure, universal categories, proven engine conventions, and cross-faction authoring standards.

order.source: Current executable catalogue and linked libraries
order.owns: What is actually deployed and how that catalogue currently implements its rules.
Engine reality when BattleScribe/New Recruit behavior differs from expectation or documentation.
Audit workflow, maintenance discipline, presentation review, rules-version update procedure, and validation process.
Current project state, recent decisions, active work, known pending issues, current file relationships, and continuity between chats.
Archaeology and rationale only. Historical state does not override current executable behavior or current doctrine.

authority_hierarchy.conflict_rule: If current sources disagree, identify the contradiction explicitly. Do not silently choose the interpretation that is easiest to implement.

semantic_source_of_truth.canonical_principle: The Universal Unit Skeleton and authoritative army rules define game meaning. New Recruit is an output format, not a source of additional semantics.
implications: New Recruit categories, groups, constraints, modifiers, and associations are implementation tools.
They must never silently redefine what a unit is, what it may take, or how a source rule works.
If the source does not contain enough information to compile a rule deterministically, fail loudly or ask for clarification rather than inventing behavior.

semantics: Never invent faction game semantics because New Recruit needs a convenient structure.
Preserve existing stable IDs whenever the same semantic object still exists.
Do not use names or display order as surrogate semantic identity when stable source IDs exist.
Never hide points or create invisible taxes.
Treat source-derived rule descriptions as source authority and preserve them verbatim unless the authoritative source changes.
new_recruit: Treat actual runtime testing as evidence.
Distinguish proven engine behavior from hypotheses.
Prefer boring, robust mechanics with constructive validation over clever structures that depend on unproven engine behavior.
Do not assume stock New Recruit constraints or messages are preferable merely because they are familiar.
maintenance: Preserve working architecture unless the source changed, a live bug exists, or a mechanical redesign is explicitly intended.
Presentation cleanup should not silently become rules redesign.
Investigate unusual structures before deleting them.
When shared content is involved, determine whether a change is intrinsic to the reusable unit tree or consumer-local before syncing libraries.

onboarding_sequence.instruction: Use this sequence for a cold start. The order is deliberate because each stage gives context needed to interpret the next one.

steps.name: Read this Pre-Introduction
steps.purpose: Establish the mental model, authority hierarchy, and project philosophy before encountering implementation detail.

steps.name: Read the current Handoff
steps.purpose: Learn current project state, active work, recent decisions, pending issues, current file relationships, and the intended pickup point.

steps.name: Research current New Recruit / BattleScribe documentation
steps.purpose: Refresh the underlying schema and engine vocabulary rather than relying on old model knowledge. Treat documentation as engine reference, not as project-specific doctrine.

steps.name: Read the current Game System and Maintenance Guide
steps.purpose: Load the project's current reusable doctrine, engine conventions, authoring rules, maintenance workflow, and validation expectations.

steps.name: Examine current representative catalogues and linked libraries
steps.purpose: See how the doctrine is actually deployed. Prefer the current files identified by the handoff rather than any historically favored faction.

steps.name: Reconcile before editing
steps.purpose: Compare the handoff, Game System, Maintenance Guide, current catalogues, linked libraries, and source rules. Call out genuine contradictions or stale guidance before changing executable data.

what_this_document_deliberately_does_not.reason: The old Pre-Introduction mixed timeless orientation with a snapshot of one particular work session. That made the document gradually stale even though its onboarding method remained successful.
excluded_from_this_layer: A fixed reference faction or reference catalogue.
Immediate next faction or implementation task.
Current filenames that are expected to change over time.
Exhaustive implementation recipes already owned by the Game System.
Routine maintenance procedure already owned by the Maintenance Guide.
what_this_document_deliberately_does_not.where_to_find_those_things: Use the current handoff for live project state, the Game System for durable doctrine, the Maintenance Guide for workflow, and the current files themselves for deployed implementation.

how_to_read_unusual_project_data.rule: A strange structure is not evidence that it is wrong. Many recurring shapes exist because simpler-looking alternatives failed in New Recruit.
before_changing_an_unfamiliar_pattern: Read the local comment and current Game System doctrine.
Check whether the shape is reused elsewhere.
Check the handoff for recent rationale or known runtime behavior.
Determine whether it owns semantics, presentation, validation, compatibility, export shape, or library identity.
If engine behavior is uncertain, identify the runtime test needed instead of pretending certainty.

rules: Executable or player-visible catalogue changes normally bump the catalogue revision.
Executable or player-visible shared Game System changes require a Game System revision bump.
Comment-only documentation cleanup does not inherently require a revision bump.
Catalogue Bugfixes record corrections to states that actually went live. Corrections to unreleased work belong in implementation history instead.
Comments are durable project knowledge when they explain current state, proven runtime behavior, or why an unusual structure exists.

with_user: Use implementation summaries rather than essays unless the task genuinely requires depth.
Do not use em dash punctuation.
When producing artifacts, provide direct download links.
When New Recruit behavior is uncertain, state what needs to be tested instead of pretending certainty.
with_project_data: Be aggressive about consistency where the underlying rules are genuinely equivalent.
Treat actual New Recruit testing as evidence.
Distinguish current authority from historical archaeology.

after_reading_the_required_sources: State the authority hierarchy in your own words.
Summarize the project philosophy in a few crisp sentences.
Identify the current project state and intended next task from the handoff and current files, not from this Pre-Introduction.
Mention any contradiction, stale guidance, missing dependency, or uncertainty that should be resolved before editing.
Do not begin a broad cleanup merely because unfamiliar structures look inconsistent.

closing_orientation.central_insight: The valuable asset is not merely the JSON. It is the accumulated knowledge about how source semantics, player-facing choices, New Recruit behavior, reusable libraries, and maintenance discipline fit together.
closing_orientation.what_to_preserve: Keep the architecture coherent, keep authority boundaries clear, preserve stable identity, and let observed New Recruit behavior drive further refinement.
closing_orientation.final_length_restatement: THERE IS NO MAXIMUM ACCEPTABLE HANDOFF SIZE. OMITTING A CRITICAL DETAIL IS MORE EXPENSIVE THAN ADDING EXTRA BYTES.
